# CONSTRUCTED INPUT, NOT A CAPTURE. No EC was read to make this file; every
# byte below was written by hand. See README.md.
# Shape: `ecrw.py dump 0x0400 0x0060` as §3's step 0 takes it, one 16-byte row
# per line, and the `0751-isolation-run` page with the battery bytes filled in.
# That set's `0751-isolation-run/` pair moves 0x0438 with a high byte of 0x00,
# so it cannot tell a little-endian assembly from a padded low byte; this pair
# moves 0x0434/0x0435 and 0x0438/0x0439 with a non-zero high byte, moves
# 0x0436 with the 0x00 high byte 0x0437 has throughout, and moves the two
# derived bytes 0x0448 and 0x0449 and 0x044C beside them, so every name the
# grader prints for that page is reached by a committed fixture. 0x043E and
# 0x044F move as the run set's do and stay context. The 2040 mA at
# 0x0434/0x0435 and the 16021 mV at 0x0438/0x0439 are the two live figures
# registers.yaml records, and the 0x0448 and 0x0449 values are those two
# divided by 100 as the bank1 writers it names would divide them on their
# selector-zero branch, so the page is internally consistent with what the
# annotation says the EC does. What is invented here is their placement and
# not the figures: registers.yaml records those two as live readings, and
# this pair is a construction that puts both of them at one moment, so the
# file is not a reading of anything. The companion after dump differs at
# every one of the addresses this header names but 0x0437, and nowhere
# else. Not a prediction that a battery reads this, or that it moved because
# of the load.
0400: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
0410: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
0420: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
0430: 00 00 00 00 f8 07 70 00 95 3e 00 00 00 00 32 00
0440: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 a0 14 00 00 75 00 00 30
0450: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
